summary.plain: Fermilab describes this as the third and final Muon g-2 result. Using data taken from 2020 to 2023 (over 2.5 times the statistics of the previous results) and combining them with the earlier results, the collaboration measured the muon's magnetic anomaly to 127 parts per billion, improving the precision of the world average by over a factor of four.
summary.technical: New data taken from 2020 to 2023 (over 2.5 times the total statistics of the previous results): aμ = 116,592,0710(162)×10⁻¹² (139 ppb) for the new datasets and 116,592,0705(148)×10⁻¹² (127 ppb) combined with the previous results; the new experimental world average, dominated by the measurements at FNAL, is aμ(exp) = 116,592,0715(145)×10⁻¹² (124 ppb). The paper says the measurements at FNAL have improved the precision on the world average by over a factor of four. Fermilab's announcement calls it the third and final result.

title: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 127 ppb
why_it_matters: Fermilab's announcement says the final result agrees with the published results from 2021 and 2023 but with a much better precision of 127 parts per billion, surpassing the original experimental design goal of 140 parts per billion.
